_comment: Operator-maintained trust intelligence. blocked_spki_sha256 holds hex SHA-256 hashes of SubjectPublicKeyInfo for keys that must never be trusted (for example intermediates distrusted by browser root programs). issuer_watch lists CAs under public incident review.

issuer_watch.name: eMudhra Global TLS Incident
issuer_watch.note: eMudhra disclosed on 21 Oct 2026 that eight intermediate CAs in its global TLS hierarchy had weak private keys, the result of a flawed key-generation ceremony on 30 Apr 2025. Google Chrome and Mozilla Root Programs blocked the affected intermediates, and eMudhra is exiting the global web PKI TLS business. Check that the chain validates against a current browser or OS trust store, verify that the certificate appears in Certificate Transparency (CT) logs, and ensure the leaf certificate was not issued by a compromised intermediate.

issuer_watch.name: WoSign / StartCom Distrusted CAs
issuer_watch.note: WoSign and StartCom were distrusted across Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Apple, and Microsoft due to backdated certificates, failure to disclose acquisition, and issuance of certificates without domain validation.

issuer_watch.name: DigiNotar Compromised Root
issuer_watch.note: DigiNotar was catastrophically breached in 2011, issuing hundreds of rogue fraudulent certificates including *.google.com used for state-sponsored man-in-the-middle surveillance before being permanently distrusted.

issuer_watch.name: CNNIC Subordinate CA Incident
issuer_watch.note: CNNIC issued an intermediate certificate to MCS Holdings, which used it to issue unauthorized man-in-the-middle certificates for Google domains.

issuer_watch.name: TrustCor Systems Distrust
issuer_watch.note: TrustCor Systems was distrusted by major browser vendors following investigations that revealed corporate and technical ties to spyware and surveillance operations.
